# Clavis Encrypt 3.10.0

## ✉️ Send with a password (free)

- Need to send a private file to someone who doesn't use Clavis, like an accountant or a family member? Right-click it → **Clavis → Send with a password…** (or **Sharing → Send files with a password…**).
- Clavis makes a locked copy named after the original and suggests a strong one-time password. Your original stays as it is.
- You get a ready-to-send message: they open the file at **clavisenc.com/open.html** on a phone or any computer, with nothing uploaded. Send the password a different way, such as a call or a text.

## 📂 Open files someone sent you

- Double-click a `.enc` file that someone locked with their own password: Clavis now notices it isn't yours and asks for that file's password instead of saying it can't open it. A copy is saved next to it.

## 🔓 Your files will always open

- The complete `.enc` file format is now public, with a free open-source decryptor that opens any of your files with just your password, even without Clavis Encrypt: **clavisenc.com/format.html**.
- And on any phone, Mac or Chromebook, **clavisenc.com/open.html** opens `.enc` files right in the browser, decrypted on the device.

## Install / upgrade

- **Windows, already installed:** the app updates itself (Settings → Updates → Check now), or download the new installer from https://clavisenc.com/download.html.
- **Microsoft Store:** the Store updates it automatically.
- **Linux:** install the new `.deb` from https://clavisenc.com/download.html.

Your vaults and settings are kept. The right-click menu updates itself the first time the new version starts.
